dna.framing_why: SOLVED, NOT GUESSED, by tools/solve_framing.py. At framing 1.0 this artifact's subject bounding box filled 52.1% of frame width and 17.8% of its height, with a subject share of 5.43%. The visible frame is 2 * PAD * radius * framing metres wide, so the box grows as 1/framing; solving for a target of 78% of the smaller-headroom dimension gives 0.23. THE ARTIFACT WAS NEVER DARK, EMPTY OR MISSING A FIXTURE - the camera was between three and eight times too far away, and the near-zero subject share this token had on record was a fact about the standpoint rather than about the axis.

stencil_quarter.description: One seeded field folded under each symmetry the family declares, with only the stored tile standing and the generated remainder left flat. A symmetry is a compression ratio. Also the artifact that found the axis name is a homonym: gradient_hunter's stencil is not this one.
